args.title: Reject non-integer TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES values instead of truncating them
args.body:
File: src/config.ts

The `int()` helper uses `Number.parseInt(raw, 10)`, which silently accepts strings like "12h" or "1h" and truncates them to 12 or 1, instead of failing. Validate that the whole string is a plain integer (e.g. with a regex or by checking `String(value) !== raw.trim()`) and throw the same "must be an integer" error for values like "12h", so a misconfigured TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES or RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES stops the service at startup rather than silently producing a much shorter lifetime.

args.title: Document what a degraded health check means for load balancer probes
args.body:
File: docs/API.md

The health check section documents the response shape and that it returns 503 only when the database is down, but doesn't spell out that a "degraded" queue still returns HTTP 200 by design (readiness only fails on a down database). Add a sentence clarifying that `status: degraded` is still a 200 and is informational (queue backlog), while 503 is the only signal that should take an instance out of rotation, so operators can configure their probes correctly.

args.title: Add a name filter to the reports list endpoint
args.body:
File: src/db/repos/reportRepo.ts

`reportRepo.list` only takes `userId`, `limit`, and `offset`, with no way to filter by name, so the `GET /reports` route (src/api/reports.ts) can't offer a search box. Add an optional `name` (substring, case-insensitive) parameter to `list`, applying it as an `ILIKE`/`lower()` condition in both the row query and the count query, and thread a `q`/`name` query parameter through the `GET /reports` route to pass it along.

args.title: Document the password validation rules for the reset confirm call
args.body:
File: docs/API.md

The reference for `POST /auth/password-reset/confirm` only shows `{ token, password }` with no mention of what makes the password valid. The validation is `z.string().min(10).max(200)` in src/api/auth.ts; document that a new password must be 10-200 characters, so the help desk can tell users why "validation failed" was returned.

args.title: Honor q-weights when picking a locale from Accept-Language
args.body:
File: src/i18n/index.ts

`pickLocale` splits the Accept-Language header on commas and returns the first supported language it finds, ignoring each part's `;q=` weight. For a header like `en;q=0.3, fr-FR;q=0.9`, it returns "en" even though French has higher priority. Parse each part's q value (default 1 when absent), sort candidates by descending q before matching against supported locales, so the highest-weighted supported language wins.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The `int()` helper in src/config.ts uses `Number.parseInt`, which truncates strings like "12h" or "1h" to 12 and 1 instead of rejecting them. That's why TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES=12h was read as 12 minutes, and RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES=1h as 1 minute, with no startup error. It should validate that the whole value is an integer and fail fast otherwise.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Looking at src/api/health.ts, this is intentional: readiness only returns 503 when the database is down; a "degraded" queue (backlog over 500 jobs) still returns HTTP 200, since the instance can still serve traffic. docs/API.md documents the response shape and the 503 case but doesn't spell out that degraded is still a 200 and purely informational, which is the missing piece for configuring the probe correctly.

file: src/i18n/index.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

`pickLocale` in src/i18n/index.ts iterates the comma-separated Accept-Language parts in header order and returns the first one it recognizes, ignoring each part's `;q=` weight entirely. For `en;q=0.3, fr-FR;q=0.9` it matches "en" first since it appears first in the string, even though French is weighted higher. It needs to parse and sort by q value before matching against supported locales.
